- Increased CI timeout for example tests and reduced sleep duration in error handling example (#760)

releases.author: steipete
releases.summary:
### Breaking

- Providers/Qwen: remove the deprecated `qwen-portal-auth` OAuth integration for `portal.qwen.ai`; migrate to Model Studio with `openclaw onboard --auth-choice modelstudio-api-key`. (#52709) Thanks @pomelo-nwu.
- Config/Doctor: drop automatic config migrations older than two months; very old legacy keys now fail validation instead of being rewritten on load or by `openclaw doctor`.

### Changes

- xAI/tools: move the bundled xAI provider to the Responses API, add first-class `x_search`, and auto-enable the xAI plugin from owned web-search and tool config so bundled Grok auth/configured search flows work without manual plugin toggles. (#56048) Thanks @huntharo.
- xAI/onboarding: let the bundled Grok web-search plugin offer optional `x_search` setup during `openclaw onboard` and `openclaw configure --section web`, including an x_search model picker with the shared xAI key.
- MiniMax: add image generation provider for `image-01` model, supporting generate and image-to-image editing with aspect ratio control. (#54487) Thanks @liyuan97.
- Plugins/hooks: add async `requireApproval` to `before_tool_call` hooks, letting plugins pause tool execution and prompt the user for approval via the exec approval overlay, Telegram buttons, Discord interactions, or the `/approve` command on any channel. The `/approve` command now handles both exec and plugin approvals with automatic fallback. (#55339) Thanks @vaclavbelak and @joshavant.
- ACP/channels: add current-conversation ACP binds for Discord, BlueBubbles, and iMessage so `/acp spawn codex --bind here` can turn the current chat into a Codex-backed workspace without creating a child thread, and document the distinction between chat surface, ACP session, and runtime workspace.
- OpenAI/apply_patch: enable `apply_patch` by default for OpenAI and OpenAI Codex models, and align its sandbox policy access with `write` permissions.
- Plugins/CLI backends: move bundled Claude CLI, Codex CLI, and Gemini CLI inference defaults onto the plugin surface, add bundled Gemini CLI backend support, and replace `gateway run --claude-cli-logs` with generic `--cli-backend-logs` while keeping the old flag as a compatibility alias.
- Plugins/startup: auto-load bundled provider and CLI-backend plugins from explicit config refs, so bundled Claude CLI, Codex CLI, and Gemini CLI message-provider setups no longer need manual `plugins.allow` entries.
- Podman: simplify the container setup around the current rootless user, install the launch helper under `~/.local/bin`, and document the host-CLI `openclaw --container <name> ...` workflow instead of a dedicated `openclaw` service user.
- Slack/tool actions: add an explicit `upload-file` Slack action that routes file uploads through the existing Slack upload transport, with optional filename/title/comment overrides for channels and DMs.
- Message actions/files: start unifying file-first sends on the canonical `upload-file` action by adding explicit support for Microsoft Teams and Google Chat, and by exposing BlueBubbles file sends through `upload-file` while keeping the legacy `sendAttachment` alias.
- Plugins/Matrix TTS: send auto-TTS replies as native Matrix voice bubbles instead of generic audio attachments. (#37080) thanks @Matthew19990919.
- CLI: add `openclaw config schema` to print the generated JSON schema for `openclaw.json`. (#54523) Thanks @kvokka.
- Config/TTS: auto-migrate legacy speech config on normal reads and secret resolution, keep legacy diagnostics for Doctor, and remove regular-mode runtime fallback for old bundled `tts.<provider>` API-key shapes.
- Memory/plugins: move the pre-compaction memory flush plan behind the active memory plugin contract so `memory-core` owns flush prompts and target-path policy instead of hardcoded core logic.
- MiniMax: trim model catalog to M2.7 only, removing legacy M2, M2.1, M2.5, and VL-01 models. (#54487) Thanks @liyuan97.
- Plugins/runtime: expose `runHeartbeatOnce` in the plugin runtime `system` namespace so plugins can trigger a single heartbeat cycle with an explicit delivery target override (e.g. `heartbeat: { target: "last" }`). (#40299) Thanks @loveyana.
- Agents/compaction: preserve the post-compaction AGENTS refresh on stale-usage preflight compaction for both immediate replies and queued followups. (#49479) Thanks @jared596.
- Agents/compaction: surface safeguard-specific cancel reasons and relabel benign manual `/compact` no-op cases as skipped instead of failed. (#51072) Thanks @afurm.
- Docs: add `pnpm docs:check-links:anchors` for Mintlify anchor validation while keeping `scripts/docs-link-audit.mjs` as the stable link-audit entrypoint. (#55912) Thanks @velvet-shark.
- Tavily: mark outbound API requests with `X-Client-Source: openclaw` so Tavily can attribute OpenClaw-originated traffic. (#55335) Thanks @lakshyaag-tavily.

### Fixes

- Agents/Anthropic: recover unhandled provider stop reasons (e.g. `sensitive`) as structured assistant errors instead of crashing the agent run. (#56639)
- Google/models: resolve Gemini 3.1 pro, flash, and flash-lite for all Google provider aliases by passing the actual runtime provider ID and adding a template-provider fallback; fix flash-lite prefix ordering. (#56567)
- OpenAI Codex/image tools: register Codex for media understanding and route image prompts through Codex instructions so image analysis no longer fails on missing provider registration or missing `instructions`. (#54829) Thanks @neeravmakwana.
- Agents/image tool: restore the generic image-runtime fallback when no provider-specific media-understanding provider is registered, so image analysis works again for providers like `openrouter` and `minimax-portal`. (#54858) Thanks @MonkeyLeeT.
- WhatsApp: fix infinite echo loop in self-chat DM mode where the bot's own outbound replies were re-processed as new inbound user messages. (#54570) Thanks @joelnishanth
- Telegram/splitting: replace proportional text estimate with verified HTML-length search so long messages split at word boundaries instead of mid-word; gracefully degrade when tag overhead exceeds the limit. (#56595)
- Telegram/delivery: skip whitespace-only and hook-blanked text replies in bot delivery to prevent GrammyError 400 empty-text crashes. (#56620)
- Telegram/send: validate `replyToMessageId` at all four API sinks with a shared normalizer that rejects non-numeric, NaN, and mixed-content strings. (#56587)
- Mistral: normalize OpenAI-compatible request flags so official Mistral API runs no longer fail with remaining `422 status code (no body)` chat errors.
- Control UI/config: keep sensitive raw config hidden by default, replace the blank blocked editor with an explicit reveal-to-edit state, and restore raw JSON editing without auto-exposing secrets. Fixes #55322.
- CLI/zsh: defer `compdef` registration until `compinit` is available so zsh completion loads cleanly with plugin managers and manual setups. (#56555)
- BlueBubbles/debounce: guard debounce flush against null message text by sanitizing at the enqueue boundary and adding an independent combiner guard. (#56573)
- Auto-reply: suppress JSON-wrapped `{"action":"NO_REPLY"}` control envelopes before channel delivery with a strict single-key detector; preserves media when text is only a silent envelope. (#56612)
- ACP/ACPX agent registry: align OpenClaw's ACPX built-in agent mirror with the latest `openclaw/acpx` command defaults and built-in aliases, pin versioned `npx` built-ins to exact versions, and stop unknown ACP agent ids from falling through to raw `--agent` command execution on the MCP-proxy path. (#28321) Thanks @m0nkmaster and @vincentkoc.
- Security/audit: extend web search key audit to recognize Gemini, Grok/xAI, Kimi, Moonshot, and OpenRouter credentials via a boundary-safe bundled-web-search registry shim. (#56540)
- Docs/FAQ: remove broken Xfinity SSL troubleshooting cross-links from English and zh-CN FAQ entries — both sections already contain the full workaround inline. (#56500)
- Telegram: deliver verbose tool summaries inside forum topic sessions again, so threaded topic chats now match DM verbose behavior. (#43236) Thanks @frankbuild.
- BlueBubbles/CLI agents: restore inbound prompt image refs for CLI routed turns, reapply embedded runner image size guardrails, and cover both CLI image transport paths with regression tests. (#51373)
- BlueBubbles/groups: optionally enrich unnamed participant lists with local macOS Contacts names after group gating passes, so group member context can show names instead of only raw phone numbers.
- Discord/reconnect: drain stale gateway sockets, clear cached resume state before forced fresh reconnects, and fail closed when old sockets refuse to die so Discord recovery stops looping on poisoned resume state. (#54697) Thanks @ngutman.
- iMessage: stop leaking inline `[[reply_to:...]]` tags into delivered text by sending `reply_to` as RPC metadata and stripping stray directive tags from outbound messages. (#39512) Thanks @mvanhorn.
- CLI/plugins: make routed commands use the same auto-enabled bundled-channel snapshot as gateway startup, so configured bundled channels like Slack load without requiring a prior config rewrite. (#54809) Thanks @neeravmakwana.
- CLI/message send: write manual `openclaw message send` deliveries into the resolved agent session transcript again by always threading the default CLI agent through outbound mirroring. (#54187) Thanks @KevInTheCloud5617.
- CLI/onboarding: show the Kimi Code API key option again in the Moonshot setup menu so the interactive picker includes all Kimi setup paths together. Fixes #54412 Thanks @sparkyrider
- Agents/status: use provider-aware context window lookup for fresh Anthropic 4.6 model overrides so `/status` shows the correct 1.0m window instead of an underreported shared-cache minimum. (#54796) Thanks @neeravmakwana.
- OpenAI/WebSocket: preserve reasoning replay metadata and tool-call item ids on WebSocket tool turns, and start a fresh response chain when full-context resend is required. (#53856) Thanks @xujingchen1996.
- OpenAI/WS: restore reasoning blocks for Responses WebSocket runs and keep reasoning/tool-call replay metadata intact so resumed sessions do not lose or break follow-up reasoning-capable turns. (#53856) Thanks @xujingchen1996.
- Agents/errors: surface provider quota/reset details when available, but keep HTML/Cloudflare rate-limit pages on the generic fallback so raw error pages are not shown to users. (#54512) Thanks @bugkill3r.
- Claude CLI: switch the bundled Claude CLI backend to `stream-json` output so watchdogs see progress on long runs, and keep session/usage metadata even when Claude finishes with an empty result line. (#49698) Thanks @felear2022.
- Claude CLI/MCP: always pass a strict generated `--mcp-config` overlay for background Claude CLI runs, including the empty-server case, so Claude does not inherit ambient user/global MCP servers. (#54961) Thanks @markojak.
- Agents/embedded replies: surface mid-turn 429 and overload failures when embedded runs end without a user-visible reply, while preserving successful media-only replies that still use legacy `mediaUrl`. (#50930) Thanks @infichen.
- Chat/UI: move the chat send button onto the shared ghost-button theme styling, while keeping the stop button icon readable on the danger state. (#55075) Thanks @bottenbenny.
- WhatsApp/allowFrom: show a specific allowFrom policy error for valid blocked targets instead of the misleading `<E.164|group JID>` format hint. Thanks @mcaxtr.
- Agents/cooldowns: scope rate-limit cooldowns per model so one 429 no longer blocks every model on the same auth profile, replace the exponential 1 min -> 1 h escalation with a stepped 30 s / 1 min / 5 min ladder, and surface a user-facing countdown message when all models are rate-limited. (#49834) Thanks @kiranvk-2011.
- Agents/embedded transport errors: distinguish common network failures like connection refused, DNS lookup failure, and interrupted sockets from true timeouts in embedded-run user messaging and lifecycle diagnostics. (#51419) Thanks @scoootscooob.
- Telegram/pairing: ignore self-authored DM `message` updates so bot-pinned status cards and similar service updates do not trigger bogus pairing requests or re-enter inbound dispatch. (#54530) thanks @huntharo
- Mattermost/replies: keep pairing replies, slash-command fallback replies, and model-picker messages on the resolved config path so `exec:` SecretRef bot tokens work across all outbound reply branches. (#48347) thanks @mathiasnagler.
- Microsoft Teams/config: accept the existing `welcomeCard`, `groupWelcomeCard`, `promptStarters`, and feedback/reflection keys in strict config validation so already-supported Teams runtime settings stop failing schema checks. (#54679) Thanks @gumclaw.
- MCP/channels: add a Gateway-backed channel MCP bridge with Codex/Claude-facing conversation tools, Claude channel notifications, and safer stdio bridge lifecycle handling for reconnects and routed session discovery.
- Plugins/SDK: thread `moduleUrl` through plugin-sdk alias resolution so user-installed plugins outside the openclaw directory (e.g. `~/.openclaw/extensions/`) correctly resolve `openclaw/plugin-sdk/*` subpath imports, and gate `plugin-sdk:check-exports` in `release:check`. (#54283) Thanks @xieyongliang.

- Message tool/buttons: keep the shared `buttons` schema optional in merged tool definitions so plain `action=send` calls stop failing validation when no buttons are provided. (#54418) Thanks @adzendo.
- Agents/openai-compatible tool calls: deduplicate repeated tool call ids across live assistant messages and replayed history so OpenAI-compatible backends no longer reject duplicate `tool_call_id` values with HTTP 400. (#40996) Thanks @xaeon2026.
- Models/openai-completions: default non-native OpenAI-compatible providers to omit tool-definition `strict` fields unless users explicitly opt back in, so tool calling keeps working on providers that reject that option. (#45497) Thanks @sahancava.
- Plugins/context engines: retry strict legacy `assemble()` calls without the new `prompt` field when older engines reject it, preserving prompt-aware retrieval compatibility for pre-prompt plugins. (#50848) thanks @danhdoan.
- CLI/update status: explicitly say `up to date` when the local version already matches npm latest, while keeping the availability logic unchanged. (#51409) Thanks @dongzhenye.
- Daemon/Linux: stop flagging non-gateway systemd services as duplicate gateways just because their unit files mention OpenClaw, reducing false-positive doctor/log noise. (#45328) Thanks @gregretkowski.
- Feishu: close WebSocket connections on monitor stop/abort so ghost connections no longer persist, preventing duplicate event processing and resource leaks across restart cycles. (#52844) Thanks @schumilin.
- Feishu: use the original message `create_time` instead of `Date.now()` for inbound timestamps so offline-retried messages carry the correct authoring time, preventing mis-targeted agent actions on stale instructions. (#52809) Thanks @schumilin.
- Control UI/Skills: open skill detail dialogs with the browser modal lifecycle so clicking a skill row keeps the panel centered instead of rendering it off-screen at the bottom of the page.
- Matrix/replies: include quoted poll question/options in inbound reply context so the agent sees the original poll content when users reply to Matrix poll messages. (#55056) Thanks @alberthild.
- Matrix/plugins: keep plugin bootstrap from crashing when built runtime mixes bare and deep `matrix-js-sdk` entrypoints, so unrelated channels do not get taken down during plugin load. (#56273) Thanks @aquaright1.
- Agents/sandbox: honor `tools.sandbox.tools.alsoAllow`, let explicit sandbox re-allows remove matching built-in default-deny tools, and keep sandbox explain/error guidance aligned with the effective sandbox tool policy. (#54492) Thanks @ngutman.
- Agents/sandbox: make blocked-tool guidance glob-aware again, redact/sanitize session-specific explain hints for safer copy-paste, and avoid leaking control-character session keys in those hints. (#54684) Thanks @ngutman.
- Agents/compaction: trigger timeout recovery compaction before retrying high-context LLM timeouts so embedded runs stop repeating oversized requests. (#46417) thanks @joeykrug.
- Agents/compaction: reconcile `sessions.json.compactionCount` after a late embedded auto-compaction success so persisted session counts catch up once the handler reports completion. (#45493) Thanks @jackal092927.
- Agents/failover: classify Codex accountId token extraction failures as auth errors so model fallback continues to the next configured candidate. (#55206) Thanks @cosmicnet.
- Plugins/runtime: reuse only compatible active plugin registries across tools, providers, web search, and channel bootstrap, align `/tools/invoke` plugin loading with the session workspace, and retry outbound channel recovery when the pinned channel surface changes so plugin tools and channels stop disappearing or re-registering from mismatched runtime loads. Thanks @gumadeiras.
- Talk/macOS: stop direct system-voice failures from replaying system speech, use app-locale fallback for shared watchdog timing, and add regression coverage for the macOS fallback route and language-aware timeout policy. (#53511) thanks @hongsw.
- Discord/gateway cleanup: keep late Carbon reconnect-exhausted errors suppressed through startup/dispose cleanup so Discord monitor shutdown no longer crashes on late gateway close events. (#55373) Thanks @Takhoffman.
- Discord/gateway shutdown: treat expected reconnect-exhausted events during intentional lifecycle stop as clean shutdowns so startup-abort cleanup no longer surfaces false gateway failures. (#55324) Thanks @joelnishanth.
- Discord/gateway shutdown: suppress reconnect-exhausted events that were already buffered before teardown flips `lifecycleStopping`, so stale-socket Discord restarts no longer crash the whole gateway. Fixes #55403 and #55421. Thanks @lml2468 and @vincentkoc.
- GitHub Copilot/auth refresh: treat large `expires_at` values as seconds epochs and clamp far-future runtime auth refresh timers so Copilot token refresh cannot fall into a `setTimeout` overflow hot loop. (#55360) Thanks @michael-abdo.
- Agents/status: use the persisted runtime session model in `session_status` when no explicit override exists, and honor per-agent `thinkingDefault` in both `session_status` and `/status`. (#55425) Thanks @scoootscooob, @xaeon2026, and @ysfbsf.
- Heartbeat/runner: guarantee the interval timer is re-armed after heartbeat runs and unexpected runner errors so scheduled heartbeats do not silently stop after an interrupted cycle. (#52270) Thanks @MiloStack.
- Config/Doctor: rewrite stale bundled plugin load paths from legacy `extensions/*` locations to the packaged bundled path, including directory-name mismatches and slash-suffixed config entries. (#55054) Thanks @SnowSky1.
- WhatsApp/mentions: stop treating mentions embedded in quoted messages as direct mentions so replying to a message that @mentioned the bot no longer falsely triggers mention gating. (#52711) Thanks @lurebat.
- Matrix: keep separate 2-person rooms out of DM routing after `m.direct` seeds successfully, while still honoring explicit `is_direct` state and startup fallback recovery. (#54890) thanks @private-peter
- Agents/ollama fallback: surface non-2xx Ollama HTTP errors with a leading status code so HTTP 503 responses trigger model fallback again. (#55214) Thanks @bugkill3r.
- Feishu/tools: stop synthetic agent ids like `agent-spawner` from being treated as Feishu account ids during tool execution, so tools fall back to the configured/default Feishu account unless the contextual id is a real enabled Feishu account. (#55627) Thanks @MonkeyLeeT.
- Google/tools: strip empty `required: []` arrays from Gemini tool schemas so optional-only tool parameters no longer trigger Google validator 400s. (#52106) Thanks @oliviareid-svg.
- Onboarding/TUI/local gateways: show the resolved gateway port in setup output, clarify no-daemon local health/dashboard messaging, and preserve loopback Control UI auth on reruns and explicit local gateway URLs so local quickstart flows recover cleanly. (#55730) Thanks @shakkernerd.
- TUI/chat log: keep system messages as single logical entries and prune overflow at whole-message boundaries so wrapped system spacing stays intact. (#55732) Thanks @shakkernerd.
- TUI/activation: validate `/activation` arguments in the TUI and reject invalid values instead of silently coercing them to `mention`. (#55733) Thanks @shakkernerd.
- Agents/model switching: apply `/model` changes to active embedded runs at the next safe retry boundary, so overloaded or retrying turns switch to the newly selected model instead of staying pinned to the old provider.
- Agents/Codex fallback: classify Codex `server_error` payloads as failoverable, sanitize `Codex error:` payloads before they reach chat, preserve context-overflow guidance for prefixed `invalid_request_error` payloads, and omit provider `request_id` values from user-facing UI copy. (#42892) Thanks @xaeon2026.
- Memory/search: share memory embedding provider registrations across split plugin runtimes so memory search no longer fails with unknown provider errors after memory-core registers built-in adapters. (#55945) Thanks @glitch418x.
- Discord/Carbon beta: update `@buape/carbon` to the latest beta and pass the new `RateLimitError` request argument so Discord stays compatible with the upstream beta constructor change. (#55980) Thanks @ngutman.
- Plugins/inbound claims: pass full inbound attachment arrays through `inbound_claim` hook metadata while keeping the legacy singular media attachment fields for compatibility. (#55452) Thanks @huntharo.
- Plugins/Matrix: preserve sender filenames for inbound media by forwarding `originalFilename` to `saveMediaBuffer`. (#55692) thanks @esrehmki.
- Matrix/mentions: recognize `matrix.to` mentions whose visible label uses the bot's room display name, so `requireMention: true` rooms respond correctly in modern Matrix clients. (#55393) thanks @nickludlam.
- Ollama/thinking off: route `thinkingLevel=off` through the live Ollama extension request path so thinking-capable Ollama models now receive top-level `think: false` instead of silently generating hidden reasoning tokens. (#53200) Thanks @BruceMacD.
- Plugins/diffs: stage bundled `@pierre/diffs` runtime dependencies during packaged updates so the bundled diff viewer keeps loading after global installs and updates. (#56077) Thanks @gumadeiras.
- Plugins/diffs: load bundled Pierre themes without JSON module imports so diff rendering keeps working on newer Node builds. (#45869) thanks @NickHood1984.
- Plugins/uninstall: remove owned `channels.<id>` config when uninstalling channel plugins, and keep the uninstall preview aligned with explicit channel ownership so built-in channels and shared keys stay intact. (#35915) Thanks @wbxl2000.
- Plugins/Matrix: prefer explicit DM signals when choosing outbound direct rooms and routing unmapped verification summaries, so strict 2-person fallback rooms do not outrank the real DM. (#56076) thanks @gumadeiras
- Plugins/Matrix: resolve env-backed `accessToken` and `password` SecretRefs against the active Matrix config env path during startup, and officially accept SecretRef `accessToken` config values. (#54980) thanks @kakahu2015.
- Microsoft Teams/proactive DMs: prefer the freshest personal conversation reference for `user:<aadObjectId>` sends when multiple stored references exist, so replies stop targeting stale DM threads. (#54702) Thanks @gumclaw.
- Gateway/plugins: reuse the session workspace when building HTTP `/tools/invoke` tool lists and harden tool construction to infer the session agent workspace by default, so workspace plugins do not re-register on repeated HTTP tool calls. (#56101) thanks @neeravmakwana
- Brave/web search: normalize unsupported Brave `country` filters to `ALL` before request and cache-key generation so locale-derived values like `VN` stop failing with upstream 422 validation errors. (#55695) Thanks @chen-zhang-cs-code.
- Discord/replies: preserve leading indentation when stripping inline reply tags so reply-tagged plain text and fenced code blocks keep their formatting. (#55960) Thanks @Nanako0129.
- Daemon/status: surface immediate gateway close reasons from lightweight probes and prefer those concrete auth or pairing failures over generic timeouts in `openclaw daemon status`. (#56282) Thanks @mbelinky.
- Agents/failover: classify HTTP 410 errors as retryable timeouts by default while still preserving explicit session-expired, billing, and auth signals from the payload. (#55201) thanks @nikus-pan.
- Agents/subagents: restore completion announce delivery for extension channels like BlueBubbles. (#56348)
- Plugins/Matrix: load bundled `@matrix-org/matrix-sdk-crypto-nodejs` through `createRequire(...)` so E2EE media send and receive keep the package-local native binding lookup working in packaged ESM builds. (#54566) thanks @joelnishanth.
- Plugins/Matrix: encrypt E2EE image thumbnails with `thumbnail_file` while keeping unencrypted-room previews on `thumbnail_url`, so encrypted Matrix image events keep thumbnail metadata without leaking plaintext previews. (#54711) thanks @frischeDaten.

issue_insights.summary_brief: 本次信号覆盖 22 个仓库，共识别 5 个跨仓库共性问题，其中 **Claude thinking_blocks 被非 Claude 提供商拒绝** 影响最广（58 个仓库），属于 P0 阻断级别；单仓层面，**GraphQL UI 组件多处崩溃**（Arize/phoenix）和 **AsyncSQLAlchemyMemory 数据库并发冲突**（agentscope）是最高影响单仓问题。
global_highlights: 【跨仓 P0】Claude thinking_blocks 在切换到 Fireworks/Together 等非 Claude LLM 时导致 BadRequestError，影响 58 个仓库的核心工作流，亟需在请求前过滤或转换 thinking_blocks 格式。
【跨仓 P0】@openrouter/ai-sdk-provider 依赖缺失导致多款 Electron 应用（Auto-Claude、opencode 等）在 Beta 版本启动时 crash，涉及 23 个仓库。
【单仓 P0】Arize/phoenix 的 GraphQL UI 在 metadata 过滤、span 详情查询、空闲冻结三个场景均崩溃，核心 trace 可观测性完全不可用。
【单仓 P0】agentscope 的 AsyncSQLAlchemyMemory 在 parallel_tool_calls 模式下并发写入触发主键冲突（3 个相关 P0 issue），多 agent 并发场景直接崩溃。

bun turbo typecheck pre-push hook failure

source_issues.evidence: npm i -g cline fails on macOS arm64 (Apple Silicon) with sharp build error. Install script fails to locate prebuilt binaries and falls back to building from source, which fails due to missing node-addon-api. Requires a manual 4-step workaround to install.

source_issues.title: perf(checkpoint-sqlite): N+1 query pattern in SqliteSaver.list() and AsyncSqliteSaver.alist()
source_issues.evidence: SqliteSaver.list() executes 101 queries (1 + 100 per checkpoint) instead of 2 queries. Demonstrated with 100 checkpoints in memory SQLite. Linear degradation: each additional checkpoint adds one extra query.

source_issues.title: Cannot install or upgrade plugin
source_issues.evidence: Plugin installation fails with 'h11 connection timeout' during uv dependency install. User cannot install or upgrade any plugin on self-hosted Docker deployment v1.13.3.

source_issues.title: Node.js SDK: Lazy-load pg to avoid ESM/CJS crash when not using pgvector
source_issues.evidence: pg is a CJS module but is statically imported in the ESM bundle as 'import { Client } from "pg"', causing SyntaxError at module load time. source_issues.evidence: ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND for '@openrouter/ai-sdk-provider' on app launch. Steps: opened app after downloading from GH, error on every launch. Release version works fine.

signals.topic: Claude thinking_blocks cause API rejection when switching to non-Claude LLM providers
signals.summary: When users switch from Claude to Fireworks/Together mid-task (e.g., due to rate limits or credit exhaustion), the conversation history contains Claude-generated thinking_blocks that non-Claude providers reject with BadRequestError, causing main workflow to fail completely.
aliases: thinking_blocks not stripped on provider switch
multi-provider switching fails with thinking blocks
signals.review_reason: Main workflow failure: provider switching is a legitimate multi-provider usage pattern but results in complete request rejection due to unstripped Claude-specific fields. LiteLLM's drop_params only handles request params, not message-level fields, so this is a genuine cross-provider compatibility gap with no workaround described. count=1 limits priority to P1.

source_issues.title: Thinking blocks compatibility for non-Claude providers
source_issues.evidence: litellm.BadRequestError from Fireworks_ai: 'Extra inputs are not permitted, field: messages[2].thinking_blocks'. Scenario: user starts with Claude (generates thinking_blocks), hits rate limit, switches to Fireworks, message history still contains thinking_blocks causing full request rejection.

signals.topic: UI filter bar crashes with GraphQL "an unexpected error occurred" when filtering on metadata keys

source_issues.title: [BUG] UI filter bar crashes with an unexpected error occurred when filtering on metadata keys
source_issues.evidence: 用户在 filter bar 中使用 metadata 过滤条件时，GraphQL 查询 'SpansTableSpansQuery' 直接返回 'an unexpected error occurred'，trace 过滤主流程被阻断。用户提供了完整复现步骤和请求体。

signals.topic: package import 时 AssertionError 导致 arize-phoenix 无法加载（FastAPI 0.115.14 不兼容）

signals.review_reason: 包导入时即抛出 AssertionError，属于最高级别阻断——用户的整个 tracing/otel 集成流程无法启动，这是主流程失败而非边缘问题。FastAPI 0.115.14 为最新稳定版，用户无升级路径，实质上阻止了特定环境用户使用 phoenix。

source_issues.title: [BUG]: UI freezes after being idle, followed by "unexpected error while fetching data" on reload

signals.topic: Mobile web UI navigation sidebar has critical UX defects — auto-opens on load/resize, cannot be reopened after dismiss, no persistent affordance
signals.summary: On mobile devices, the sidebar navigation auto-opens as a full-screen overlay on every page load and on window resize, covering the actual content the user wants to see. Once dismissed, there is no way (no hamburger button, no bottom tab bar, no swipe gesture) to reopen the navigation, leaving users permanently unable to access conversations, tasks, or settings on mobile.
signals.review_reason: 这是移动端用户在真实场景下反复遭遇的体验阻断问题：每次打开应用或调整窗口大小时，导航侧边栏自动弹出让用户看不到聊天内容；一旦关闭后，没有任何交互方式（汉堡菜单、底部标签栏或滑动手势）能重新打开导航，导致核心功能（对话列表、任务、历史记录、设置）永久不可访问。该问题有明确的根因定位（leftSidebarVisible$ 默认 true，桌面布局的 expand() 在切换到移动端后状态未重置，移动端布局完全缺少重新打开导航的触发器），且经 repo owner 确认并已合并修复，确认为用户痛点而非边缘情况。

source_issues.title: webui: mobile navigation sidebar UX needs rethinking

signals.topic: MCP tool initialization timeout leaves agent in zombie state with no user-facing error

This is a main-flow blocking issue even though the UI appears responsive. The absence of any error state means users cannot diagnose or recover from the failure.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: Observed Behavior: The agent remains idle. No visual feedback or error notification is shown in the interface.

signals.topic: Self-hosted UI stuck on Starting/Loading screen despite backend being fully ready

source_issues.title: [Bug]: V0 conversations have additional trailing characters in metadata.json

source_issues.title: BlockUnknownError: raised by AITextGeneratorBlock with message: Error calling LLM: No content returned from Anthropic
source_issues.evidence: AITextGeneratorBlock 在调用 Anthropic LLM 时返回空内容，block 抛出 BlockUnknownError，agent 主流程被阻断

signals.topic: AsyncSQLAlchemyMemory 并发写入时触发数据库主键冲突错误，导致 parallel_tool_calls 模式下主流程崩溃
signals.summary: 当 ReActAgent 开启 parallel_tool_calls=True 并使用 AsyncSQLAlchemyMemory 时，多个并发工具调用同时执行会导致多个 _acting 协程同时调用 memory.add()，触发 IntegrityError: Duplicate entry 主键冲突错误，进程崩溃/阻断。
signals.review_reason: 用户直接遭遇数据库完整性错误（IntegrityError: Duplicate entry），进程崩溃且需手动清理消息才能恢复，是典型的主流程阻断性 bug。错误路径清晰（parallel_tool_calls + AsyncSQLAlchemyMemory），有完整堆栈和 SQL 语句证据，P0 成立。

source_issues.title: [Bug]:Duplicate Entry Error in AsyncSQLAlchemyMemory with parallel_tool_calls=True
source_issues.evidence: sqlalchemy.exc.IntegrityError: (1062, "Duplicate entry '...' for key 'PRIMARY'")，多条并发工具调用同时写 memory.add() 触发主键冲突，进程崩溃，需清除消息才能恢复。

signals.topic: AsyncSQLAlchemyMemory 使用 structured_model 时出现外键约束错误，导致消息存储失败
signals.summary: 在 AsyncSQLAlchemyMemory.add() 方法中，session.add() 仅将消息标记为待插入（内存态），而 bulk_insert_mappings() 立即执行 SQL 写 message_mark 表，此时消息尚未真正写入数据库，外键约束失败，导致 PendingRollbackError，主流程阻断。
signals.review_reason: 外键约束错误直接导致消息无法持久化，Session 进入 rollback 状态，用户必须重建 Session 才能继续，是主流程阻断性 bug。根因定位清晰（缺 flush），用户影响明确，P0 成立。

source_issues.title: [Bug]:Foreign Key Constraint Error when using structured_model in AsyncSQLAlchemyMemory
source_issues.evidence: sqlalchemy.exc.PendingRollbackError: foreign key constraint fails (message_mark.msg_id references message.id which doesn't exist yet)。根因分析清晰：session.add() 延迟写入，但 bulk_insert_mappings() 立即执行，未 flush 导致外键断裂。

source_issues.title: [Possible Bug] False-positive bans when using Claude Code Action for intensive PR review loops

signals.topic: GHES MCP server TLS/CA certificate trust not configurable — action non-functional on corporate GHES
signals.summary: On GitHub Enterprise Server instances using internal/private CA certificates (self-signed or corporate CA), the GitHub MCP server Docker container fails all API calls with TLS certificate verification errors. There is no configuration option to mount custom CA certificates, override the Docker image, or pass additional Docker arguments, making the action completely non-functional in corporate environments where internal CAs are standard.
aliases: GHES internal CA certificate MCP server
TLS trust CA certificates GHES self-hosted runners
signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断：MCP server 是 action 的核心组件，在使用内部 CA 证书的企业版 GHES 环境下完全失效。由于没有配置项可以绕过或修复，所有使用 MCP server 工具 (mcp__github__*) 的工作流都会失败，等效于企业用户的关键功能不可用。虽然 count=1，但企业内部 CA 环境极为普遍，且提供了明确的 root cause 和 minimal fix，置信度极高，定 P1。

source_issues.title: GitHub MCP server fails on GHES with internal CA certificates — no way to configure TLS trust
source_issues.evidence: Action is completely non-functional on any GHES instance with internal CA certificates. Every MCP server API call fails with 'tls: failed to verify certificate: x509: certificate signed by unknown authority'. This affects a standard corporate setup (internal CAs are extremely common in enterprise environments). Self-hosted runner itself trusts GHE server for job dispatch, so the fix is trivial (mount host CA bundle), but no workaround exists currently.

signals.topic: SDK execution file not written on rate limit errors — prevents workflow error differentiation
signals.summary: When Claude Code hits a rate limit, the SDK throws after writing the rate_limit_event to the messages array, but because the execution file write in run-claude-sdk.ts is after the try/catch block (not in finally), the file is never written. This means workflows using continue-on-error: true cannot distinguish rate limits from other failures, making it impossible to post targeted warnings, surface reset times, or skip redundant re-runs.
aliases: execution file not written on error
signals.review_reason: 影响自动化工作流的错误处理能力：workflow 无法区分 rate limit 和其他错误类型，导致无法智能处理限流场景（如等待重试、展示重置时间）。虽然没有直接阻断主流程，但严重影响了依赖 action 做自动化错误处理的用户的体验，属于明显的体验下降。

source_issues.title: Write execution file in finally block so rate limit errors are parseable
source_issues.evidence: The messages array is populated before the throw (including rate_limit_event), but the execution file write is unreachable after the throw in the catch block. Callers cannot distinguish rate limits from other failures — both surface as exit code 1 with a minified SDK stack trace. Workflows that rely on execution_file output for post-processing cannot function for rate limit scenarios.

The review text was generated in an earlier turn, but the result capture does not pick it up, so no comment is ever posted to the PR despite the action running for ~7 minutes and completing successfully.

signals.topic: Cron/scheduled jobs silently skipped when container is suspended or asleep
signals.summary: OpenClaw internal cron scheduler runs inside the container, but containers get suspended during idle periods, freezing the Node.js event loop and causing all scheduled tasks (daily briefs, weekly reports) to be silently skipped.
signals.review_reason: 两个 issue 描述同一场景：容器空闲挂起后内部定时器停止，导致 cron 任务静默跳过。#250 提供了清晰的用户证据（Gateway 运行数小时但 cron 执行数为零，手动触发正常）。关键功能（定时任务）不可用，但用户仍可通过外部请求唤醒容器，属于体验下降而非完全阻断，定级 P1。

source_issues.evidence: Container sleeps after inactivity when SANDBOX_SLEEP_AFTER is set. Cron job scheduled for 07:30 is skipped because container is asleep. signals.review_reason: Gateway 启动即失败，导致容器内核心服务（OpenClaw 网关）不可用。用户无法正常使用 bot 功能，属于主流程阻断。虽然 count=1（单仓单 issue），但提供了明确的根因分析、复现步骤和错误日志，且网关启动失败是核心功能的前置依赖，定级 P1。

Attaching files directly to task still works, proving input_files path is the broken code path.

signals.topic: Shared LLM stop words mutation causes cross-agent state pollution in multi-agent crews
signals.summary: When multiple agents share the same LLM instance, CrewAgentExecutor.__init__ mutates the shared LLM's stop attribute, causing stop words to accumulate monotonically across agents and pollute each other's generation behavior. Also a race condition in async execution.
aliases: LLM stop words accumulate across agents
stop words grow monotonically across kickoff calls
signals.review_reason: Experience degradation in production multi-agent crews: stop words accumulate monotonically across agents sharing an LLM instance. Silent behavioral degradation — no error raised, LLM just terminates prematurely with wrong output. Includes documented race condition in async execution. Code comment explicitly acknowledges the bug. Affects the default/common case of 2+ agents sharing an LLM.

source_issues.title: [Bug] Shared LLM stop words mutation causes cross-agent state pollution
source_issues.evidence: Code in crew_agent_executor.py lines 164-173 mutates self.llm.stop directly. Existing comment acknowledges: 'This may be mutating the shared llm object and needs further evaluation.' Impact: Agent A adds stop words, Agent B inherits A+B stop words, Agent C inherits A+B+C. Stop words never cleaned up after agent finishes. Extra stop words cause premature LLM termination. Race condition in async when multiple agents mutate simultaneously. Affects all crews with 2+ agents sharing LLM (the default/common case).

signals.topic: litellm multi-provider routing broken — base_url not mapped to api_base and agent internals bypass LLM credentials
signals.summary: CrewAI 1.12.x with litellm provider fails LLM calls with AuthenticationError because LLM(base_url=...) stores URL in base_url but litellm reads from api_base which remains None. Additionally, agent internal calls bypass LLM object params and fall back to global env vars, breaking multi-provider setups.
aliases: litellm authentication fails with custom base_url
api_base None causes fallback to OpenAI default
signals.review_reason: Main flow blocking: LLM calls fail with litellm.AuthenticationError due to base_url not mapped to api_base. Breaks multi-provider production setups (Scaleway+Nebius) which is an enterprise use case. Agent internal calls (tool selection, reasoning) bypass LLM credentials entirely, falling back to global env vars. Two distinct root causes documented with reproduction steps and evidence of API key being sent to wrong endpoint.

source_issues.title: [BUG] fix: CrewAI 1.12.x LLM routing - litellm does not receive api_base/api_key for multi-provider setups
source_issues.evidence: litellm.AuthenticationError: requests sent to api.openai.com instead of Scaleway endpoint, Scaleway API key rejected by OpenAI. Root cause: LLM(base_url=X) sets self.base_url=X but self.api_base=None. CrewAI agent internal litellm calls (tool selection, reasoning) do not pass api_key/api_base from LLM object, fall back to global env vars. Multi-provider setup (Scaleway+Nebius) cannot work — global env var can only serve one provider. crewai[litellm]~=1.12.0, Ubuntu 3.10.

signals.topic: MCPToolResolver UnboundLocalError crash when native MCP config returns zero tools
signals.summary: MCPToolResolver._resolve_native() silently returns empty tool list when MCP server returns no tools or tool_filter removes all tools, then crashes with UnboundLocalError at tool_resolver.py line 412. No warning logged, making debugging impossible.
aliases: no warning for zero MCP tools
MCP server returns no tools crash
signals.review_reason: Main flow blocking: MCP server returning zero tools (via empty server or aggressive tool_filter) causes UnboundLocalError crash. No warning is logged, making it nearly impossible for users to diagnose why their MCP server provides no tools. Full stacktrace confirms crash. Contrast with _resolve_external() path which does log a warning — the native path is strictly worse.

source_issues.title: [BUG] MCPToolResolver does not log warning when native MCP config returns no tools

Crash occurs when MCP server returns no tools or tool_filter removes all tools. No warning logged unlike _resolve_external() path. Full stacktrace provided. Affects MCPServerStdio, MCPServerHTTP, MCPServerSSE. Ubuntu 3.12.

signals.topic: result_as_answer=True ignores tool failure — error output becomes agent's final answer
signals.summary: When result_as_answer=True is set on a tool, the agent uses the tool's output as its final answer regardless of whether the tool succeeded or failed. Tool errors (e.g. code execution failures) get treated as valid responses, removing the agent's ability to reflect on and recover from tool failures.

source_issues.title: OSError when AGENTS.md is a symbolic link
source_issues.evidence: CLI crashes with OSError(ELOOP: too many levels of symbolic links) when AGENTS.md is a symlink to another file. O_NOFOLLOW flag introduced for security is too restrictive.

signals.topic: Summarization offload fails on Windows due to CRLF/LF line ending mismatch, causing data loss
signals.summary: On Windows, SummarizationMiddleware fails to offload conversation history after first successful write. signals.review_reason: Data integrity issue with confirmed data loss: conversation history becomes unrecoverable after the first summarization offload on Windows. source_issues.title: Summarization offload fails on Windows due to CRLF/LF mismatch
source_issues.evidence: download_files() preserves CRLF line endings from the file while edit() reads text that normalizes to LF on Windows. The string-matching logic in the offload append/edit path fails, causing 'String not found in file' error and making older messages unrecoverable.

source_issues.title: CompiledSubAgent with custom StateGraph causes infinite loop when last message is ToolMessage

signals.topic: SqliteSaver.list() and AsyncSqliteSaver.alist() execute N+1 queries (1 per checkpoint for writes), degrading linearly with checkpoint count
signals.summary: SqliteSaver.list() and AsyncSqliteSaver.alist() execute a separate writes query for every checkpoint row returned. With N checkpoints, this results in N+1 total queries instead of 2. Performance degrades linearly with checkpoint count, causing significant slowdowns and increased database load in production.
signals.review_reason: Performance regression: classic N+1 query pattern causes O(N) database queries instead of O(1). With typical checkpoint counts, users experience severe slowdowns and excessive database load. Provided reproducible test showing 101 queries for 100 checkpoints. Impacts production checkpoint retrieval, which is a high-frequency operation.

source_issues.title: perf(checkpoint-sqlite): N+1 query pattern in SqliteSaver.list() and AsyncSqliteSaver.alist()
source_issues.evidence: SqliteSaver.list() executes 101 queries (1 + 100 per checkpoint) instead of 2 queries. Demonstrated with 100 checkpoints in memory SQLite. Linear degradation: each additional checkpoint adds one extra query.

signals.topic: get_state().next returns empty tuple after a node calls interrupt() twice, causing graph state to appear complete when it is still waiting for input

source_issues.title: Node.js SDK: Lazy-load pg to avoid ESM/CJS crash when not using pgvector

signals.topic: Memory extraction pipeline produces 97.8% junk entries in production deployments
signals.summary: Production audit of 10,134 entries shows 97.8% are junk (boot files, system noise, hallucinated profiles); feedback loop amplifies hallucinations; no quality gate between extraction and storage

Harvard D3 research confirms 'indiscriminate memory storage performs worse than using no memory at all'.

source_issues.title: What we found after auditing 10,134 mem0 entries: 97.8% were junk
source_issues.evidence: 32-day production audit with 10,134 entries: 97.8% junk. Core value proposition of mem0 is fundamentally broken for production use.

signals.topic: ThreadPoolExecutor leak causes memory exhaustion and OOM kills under sustained traffic
signals.summary: Per-call ThreadPoolExecutor creation in search/add/get_all never properly cleaned up; production FastAPI servers accumulate 800+ idle threads over 8 hours, leading to OOM-killed pods
signals.review_reason: Clear main flow blocking in production: servers get OOM-killed after 8 hours of normal traffic. Thread accumulation causes memory exhaustion leading to pod failures. Production impact evidenced by thread tracer confirming new threads per call. This is a critical infrastructure reliability issue for any sustained-deployment user.

source_issues.title: Thread leak: ThreadPoolExecutor created per call in search/add/get_all, never properly cleaned up
source_issues.evidence: Production FastAPI + uvicorn deployment on Kubernetes. Thread count grows at ~1/minute under ~50 req/s. After 8 hours: 800+ idle threads, each ~10MB VmData. Pods hit memory limits and get OOM-killed. Root cause: Memory.search(), Memory.add(), Memory.get_all() each create a new ThreadPoolExecutor per call via 'with concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor()' which doesn't properly clean up threads, especially with Sentry threading integration.

signals.topic: Qdrant datetime range filtering silently returns zero results due to Range vs DatetimeRange type mismatch
signals.summary: Official documented time-based filtering examples silently return 0 results on Qdrant backend; errors swallowed by asyncio.gather with return_exceptions=True
signals.review_reason: Significant experience degradation: official documentation examples silently fail, returning 0 results with no error indication. Users relying on time-based filtering (a core use case for memory management) get completely wrong results. The error is swallowed so users don't even know filtering failed.

source_issues.title: bug: Qdrant adapter uses Range instead of DatetimeRange for datetime fields — silently returns 0 results
source_issues.evidence: The documented time-based filtering example from official docs ('created_at': {'gte': '2024-01-01T00:00:00Z'}) silently returns 0 results on Qdrant backend. Root cause: _build_field_condition always uses numeric Range for range filters, but datetime values fail pydantic validation or cannot match datetime-indexed string values. Errors are swallowed by asyncio.gather with return_exceptions=True, resulting in 0 results with no error.

signals.topic: autoRecall hook does not fire for interactive sessions, silently failing memory injection
signals.summary: before_agent_start hook used for autoRecall only fires for cron/heartbeat sessions, NOT for interactive Telegram messages; memories silently not injected for interactive users
signals.review_reason: Main flow blocking for interactive sessions: autoRecall is a core feature of the OpenClaw plugin, and it silently fails for the primary use case (interactive Telegram messages). source_issues.title: openclaw-mem0 v0.4.0: autoRecall silent failure — `before_agent_start` hook does not fire for interactive sessions
source_issues.evidence: The before_agent_start hook used for autoRecall only fires for cron/heartbeat sessions, NOT for interactive Telegram messages. Previous gateway process showed it working before restart, confirming the behavioral regression.

signals.topic: Sub-agent approval response fails to resume tool execution (multi-agent workflow blocking)

signals.review_reason: Blocks multi-agent approval workflows end-to-end. Tool never executes after user approval despite correct propagation. Affects core approval_mode feature used in controlled environments.

source_issues.title: Python: [Bug]: Cannot approve tool usage from sub-agents
source_issues.evidence: Approval response is sent but inner tool never executes. Code sample shows approval request surfaces correctly but after sending approval_response(True) the agent returns without executing the tool. Affects both .as_tool() and Workflow.as_tool(). Reproducible in both streaming and non-streaming.

signals.topic: MCP client enters infinite reconnect loop when server lacks 'ping' method support

aliases: MCP ping not supported infinite reconnect
signals.review_reason: Infinite reconnect loop causes complete app hang with no recovery. Every connection attempt to non-ping-capable MCP servers dead-locks the client. Real production impact confirmed with Snowflake managed MCP.

source_issues.title: Python: [Bug]: MCP client connection goes into infinite loop if MCP server doesn't support 'ping' method
source_issues.evidence: Full log trace shows repeating pattern: 'MCP connection invalid or closed. Reconnecting...' with HTTP 200 OK per cycle. Confirmed against Snowflake MCP server. Blocks any MCP server that doesn't implement ping method.

signals.topic: SelectorGroupChat livelock when allow_repeated_speaker=False

The bug has a clear root cause in source code and a reproduction case.

source_issues.title: [Bug] SelectorGroupChat livelock: fallback returns excluded previous speaker when allow_repeated_speaker=False
source_issues.evidence: Bug report with reproduction code showing that when LLM consistently selects the previous speaker within max_selector_attempts, the fallback returns the excluded speaker, violating allow_repeated_speaker=False and causing infinite loop. Root cause identified in _selector_group_chat.py: fallback returns self._previous_speaker when it should select a different participant.

signals.topic: Tool call ID exceeds API maximum length causing BadRequestError

This is a direct, visible failure of the main agent execution loop with concrete user impact.

source_issues.title: Tool id string too long
source_issues.evidence: Full stack trace showing openai.BadRequestError: Invalid 'messages[3].tool_calls[0].id': string too long. Expected a string with maximum length 40, but got a string with length 41 instead. signals.topic: ffmpeg child process orphaned and Node.js process hangs when no frames are recorded

source_issues.title: [Bug]: ffmpeg orphaned if no frames are recorded
source_issues.evidence: Node.js process hangs indefinitely because ffmpeg child process is orphaned waiting for stdin. Bug confirmed fixed in main branch (commit d039c403). Reproduction steps provided with repro repo. Intermittent hangs reported in production (cloudflare/telescope).

signals.topic: video-start/video-stop produces 0-byte .webm files when page navigations occur during recording

The recording produces a misleading 0-byte file rather than a clear error, making the failure silent and confusing.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: Trace viewer fails to open trace: Could not load trace from
source_issues.evidence: Explicit error 'Could not load trace from' shown to user. signals.topic: TextChunker.SplitPlainTextParagraphs silently produces oversized chunks due to word-count vs token-count mismatch

signals.review_reason: This causes silent data corruption in RAG pipelines — the TextChunker silently produces oversized chunks that corrupt embedding generation and reranking. source_issues.title: TextChunker.SplitPlainTextParagraphs sometimes overcount the chunk sizes

signals.topic: Google AI connector leaks Gemini internal thinking/reasoning text into application-visible ChatMessageContent

source_issues.evidence: Runtime crash when Npgsql 10.0.2 is used with Microsoft.SemanticKernel.Connectors.PgVector. Call to CollectionExistsAsync() throws MissingMethodException. Also affects users combining Entity Framework and PgVector.

signals.topic: OpenAIResponseAgent ignores ResponseFormat setting — structured outputs (JSON Schema) do not work

source_issues.evidence: Changing one thread from Custom (config.toml) to Full Access appears to change every active thread to full access, including threads in other projects, even threads doing unrelated work.

input_image type not supported by Chat Completions API

source_issues.evidence: User reports requests never reach Azure OpenAI when using type: image_url with Chat Completions API; switching to input_image makes requests go through but Chat Completions API does not support that format. Clear API format mismatch.

signals.topic: LitellmModel sends OpenAI-style dict reasoning_effort to non-OpenAI providers causing silent parameter ignoring
signals.summary: LitellmModel constructs dict-valued reasoning_effort {'effort': 'low', 'summary': 'auto'} for all LiteLLM providers when reasoning.summary is set. This OpenAI-only shape is not understood by non-OpenAI providers (e.g. Anthropic via LiteLLM), causing the parameter to be silently ignored instead of being properly transformed.
aliases: reasoning.summary ignored for non-OpenAI LiteLLM providers
signals.review_reason: 跨提供商兼容性问题: reasoning.summary功能在通过LitellmModel使用非OpenAI提供商时被静默忽略，用户不会收到任何错误提示，导致功能实际不可用。根因和影响链路已完整溯源。

source_issues.title: LitellmModel sends dict-valued reasoning_effort to non-OpenAI providers when reasoning.summary is set
source_issues.evidence: Source-level repro traced to litellm_model.py:446-455; LiteLLM Anthropic transformer only handles string-valued reasoning_effort; dict shape is silently ignored. SDK is the component deciding to send OpenAI-only dict shape to all providers.

signals.topic: Responses API multi-turn conversations fail on turn 2 due to model_dump() fabricating null fields (status/encrypted_content) in output items passed back as input
signals.summary: model_dump() on response.output items generates null fields (status: None, encrypted_content: None) for fields the API never returned, causing 400 'Unknown parameter' errors when those items are passed back as input in subsequent conversation turns. Breaks the fundamental multi-turn conversation pattern.
signals.review_reason: High-frequency (2 issues, cross-repo evidence) + primary use case (multi-turn conversation) completely blocked on turn 2 with 400 errors. OpenClaw (64.9k forks) broken in production. Root cause in openai/openai-openapi#536, no fix shipped since Aug 2025 (#2561 open).

source_issues.title: Responses API: multi-turn conversations 400 on turn 2 when passing response.output back as input
source_issues.evidence: model_dump() on output items produces 'status: None', 'encrypted_content: None'. API rejects null unknown parameters with 400. Affects reasoning models (o4-mini, gpt-5.3-codex). Breaks the standard pattern of passing conversation history back to the API.

source_issues.title: Responses API: undocumented reasoning+message pairing constraint breaks multi-turn conversations
source_issues.evidence: 400 error on turn 2: 'Item msg_... of type message was provided without its required preceding item of type reasoning'. Common pattern of filtering output to keep only messages silently produces orphaned items. Breaks OpenClaw (64.9k forks) on gpt-5.3-codex in production. Affects all 5 SDKs (Python, JS, Go, Java, .NET).

signals.topic: jiter library corrupts tool call arguments by converting escaped double-quotes (\") to escaped single-quotes (\'), producing invalid JSON that cannot be parsed
signals.summary: The jiter dependency in the SDK converts escaped double-quotes in tool call arguments strings to escaped single-quotes during deserialization, corrupting the JSON string. json.loads() fails on the corrupted output, breaking all function calling use cases.
signals.review_reason: Key feature (function/tool calling) produces corrupted JSON output making arguments unparseable. Breaks Home Assistant ecosystem integrations with local LLM servers. Workaround requires manual string replacement before json.loads(). The issue was closed but the core jiter corruption remains a valid user pain point.

source_issues.title: Tool call arguments field has escaped double-quotes converted to single-quotes by jiter
source_issues.evidence: SDK v2.21.0 corrupts arguments string: '\"' becomes "\'" in the deserialized output. json.loads() fails or produces wrong results. Raw HTTP (curl) returns correct JSON. Breaks the entire Home Assistant ecosystem where integrations use the SDK to communicate with llama.cpp, vLLM, Ollama for smart home control. Reproduced on both stream=True and stream=False.

signals.topic: Web fetch tool silently drops all content inside custom HTML elements (web components), returning only the page title with no error or warning
signals.summary: The web fetch functionality treats unknown HTML element names (custom elements, web components) as opaque blocks and skips their entire subtree. Any site using Angular, Lit, or web components is completely unreadable, with silent data loss and no indication to the user.
signals.review_reason: Silent data loss in a key feature (web fetch) with no error or warning. The issue describes behavior confirmed across both claude.ai and ChatGPT, likely rooted in shared upstream HTML-to-markdown library. Note: the issue is filed against the Python library but the evidence points to platform-level behavior shared across multiple OpenAI products.

source_issues.title: AI Web Fetch Tools Silently Drop Content Inside Custom HTML Elements
source_issues.evidence: Confirmed on claude.ai and ChatGPT web fetch. Pages using web components return only the <title> tag with all content silently dropped. curl, Grok, Google crawler, Claude Code WebFetch all correctly read the same pages. Root cause is non-conformant HTML parsing that skips unknown element children. No error or warning is shown to the user.

signals.topic: Response.output_text property raises TypeError when API returns null text field in output_text content items
signals.summary: The output_text property on Response objects attempts string concatenation on content items whose text field is null (returned by models like openai/gpt-oss-safeguard-120b), causing a TypeError crash. This violates the expected API contract where text should be a string or absent.
signals.review_reason: Convenience property crash (TypeError) when a model returns null text in output_text items. Non-blocking for users who avoid the output_text property, but a clear regression for those relying on it. The fix is a simple null guard.

source_issues.title: Response.output_text fails to handle null text values in content items
source_issues.evidence: TypeError crash when accessing output_text property. Model returns output_text content items with text: null. The output_text property iterates and appends to a list without null-checking, causing concatenation failure. Reproducible on openai/gpt-oss-safeguard-120b and likely other models.

signals.topic: ResponseOutputMessageParam TypedDict requires 'id' field at type-check time despite not being used or required by the API at runtime
signals.summary: Type-checkers enforce an 'id' field in ResponseOutputMessageParam even though the field is not sent to the API and has no runtime purpose for client-generated messages. Forces developers to use cast() or # type: ignore workarounds.
signals.review_reason: Developer experience friction causing type-checking errors and forcing workarounds (cast/type: ignore). While no runtime crash occurs, the SDK type definitions are inconsistent (total=False vs Required fields) and create real friction for developers building with the Responses API.

source_issues.title: Make ResponseOutputMessageParam.id genuinely optional and support message payloads without an OpenAI‑generated ID
source_issues.evidence: Type-checkers (Pylance, MyPy) require 'id' field which is not used at runtime or sent to API. Developers must use cast() or # type: ignore workarounds. The TypedDict is defined as total=False but fields are wrapped in Required[...], making id effectively required.

signals.topic: Windows agent spawn fails with EINVAL on Node.js v22 due to missing shell:true — all ACP agent commands blocked
signals.summary: On Windows with Node.js v22.12+, acpx fails to spawn any ACP agent (Codex, Claude, OpenCode, Gemini) because child_process.spawn() without shell:true cannot execute .cmd/.ps1 wrapper scripts. This was introduced as a security change in Node.js v22.12+. All agent commands are completely broken.
signals.review_reason: Two confirmed issues (#191, #169) document complete workflow blockage for Windows users on Node.js v22+. The spawn call lacks shell:true, causing EINVAL for .cmd/.ps1 wrappers and ENOENT for PATH-resolved commands. Both issue authors confirm zero agent commands work. This is a primary flow failure affecting all Windows + Node.js v22 users of acpx.

source_issues.title: Bug: spawn EINVAL on Windows with Node.js v22 — all agent commands fail
source_issues.evidence: All agent commands fail with EINVAL; acpx bundled with OpenClaw; affects every ACP agent (Codex, Claude, OpenCode, Gemini) on Windows + Node.js v22. Workaround requires downgrading to Node.js v20 or switching to HTTP API mode.

source_issues.title: Windows: terminal commands fail with ENOENT because buildTerminalSpawnOptions lacks shell:true
source_issues.evidence: buildTerminalSpawnOptions() missing shell:true on Windows causes ENOENT for all terminal commands (git, node, cmd, etc.). Spawn without shell:true cannot resolve PATH on Windows. Closed with fix merged.

signals.topic: Cursor ACP session/load fallback not triggered — -32602 error causes session failure or crash
signals.summary: acpx's shouldFallbackToNewSession() does not recognize JSON-RPC error code -32602 (Invalid params) returned by Cursor CLI for session/load failures. This prevents the automatic fallback to session/new, causing Cursor ACP sessions to fail or crash on reconnect attempts in prompt mode.
signals.review_reason: Two issues (#161, #152) confirm the same root cause: -32602 error code from Cursor's session/load is not recognized in shouldFallbackToNewSession, blocking the fallback to session/new. This causes session failures on reconnect attempts and crashes in prompt mode. Cursor is a supported ACP agent; its session persistence is broken.

source_issues.title: Cursor ACP session/load fallback not triggered due to unrecognized error code
source_issues.evidence: Cursor CLI returns -32602 with message 'Session "xxx" not found' for session/load. acpx's shouldFallbackToNewSession only handles -32002 and -32603, causing Cursor sessions to fail. Workaround: use acpx cursor exec directly (bypasses session/load). Both issues #161 and #152 are open/closed variants of the same root cause.

source_issues.title: shouldFallbackToNewSession does not handle -32602 from session/load, causing crash with cursor-agent
source_issues.evidence: cursor-agent with prompt mode crashes on reconnect: shouldFallbackToNewSession doesn't handle -32602, error propagates up uncaught causing exit code 1. exec mode works because it always uses session/new. Prompt mode (persistent sessions) fails on second run.

signals.topic: ACP session spawn silently fails and enters unrecoverable dead loop after gateway restart
signals.summary: After a gateway restart, ACP sessions permanently fail to re-establish. The error handling swallows all errors (returning null) and recoverEnsureFailure incorrectly treats null as 'session already exists', counting failed attempts as resolved. Sessions enter an infinite dead recovery loop that never recovers.
aliases: error swallowing null treated as success
acp session dead loop after restart
signals.review_reason: Gateway restart is a routine operational action; ACP sessions failing permanently afterward with zero recovery is a main flow failure. The three-layer error swallowing bug (createNamedSession→ensureSession→recoverEnsureFailure) means users cannot restart their gateway without manual intervention. The 'resolved=0 failed=N' log confirms all sessions fail silently without user notification.

source_issues.title: ACP session spawn fails silently after gateway restart — error swallowing leads to dead session loop
source_issues.evidence: After gateway restart, acpx exits with code 3 (TIMEOUT); all sessions marked dead; acp startup identity reconcile reports resolved=0 failed=N. Three-layer error swallowing bug: createNamedSession returns null on all errors, ensureSession passes null upward, recoverEnsureFailure treats null as session already exists. Sessions never recover; system enters infinite retry loop.

signals.topic: Persistent ACP sessions immediately report dead (queue owner unavailable) on macOS — thread-bound sessions unusable
signals.summary: On macOS, persistent acpx sessions become 'dead / queue owner unavailable' immediately after creation. Sessions are successfully created but immediately die, making thread-bound ACP sessions completely unusable. One-shot ACP mode works as a workaround.
aliases: macOS persistent session queue owner unavailable
acpx session dead immediately macOS arm64
queue owner health probe race condition
signals.review_reason: Persistent sessions are a core acpx feature. The queue owner becoming unavailable immediately after creation makes the entire persistent session feature unusable on macOS. OpenClaw downstream logs confirm the issue. The workaround of switching to one-shot mode defeats the purpose of persistent sessions.

source_issues.title: Persistent sessions become dead immediately (queue owner unavailable) on macOS
source_issues.evidence: sessions ensure succeeds but status immediately returns dead/queue owner unavailable. Downstream OpenClaw logs confirm: acpx ensureSession replacing dead named session. Root cause appears to be queue owner process exit immediately after session creation or health probe incorrectly marking live owner as dead. Thread-bound ACP sessions are currently unstable on macOS.

signals.topic: ACP handshake fails with Gemini CLI due to protocolVersion type mismatch (string vs number)

aliases: Gemini CLI ACP protocolVersion type mismatch
Gemini CLI handshake fails number vs string
signals.review_reason: ACP handshake failure with Gemini CLI is a clear protocol compatibility issue that blocks a specific supported agent. The type mismatch (string vs number) is well-documented and reproducible. This makes Gemini CLI + acpx integration completely non-functional.

source_issues.title: ACP: protocolVersion type mismatch with Gemini CLI (--acp)
source_issues.evidence: acpx sends protocolVersion as string '1.0'; Gemini CLI strictly requires number 1. Handshake fails with -32603 invalid_type error. Codex and Claude work fine with acpx; only Gemini CLI is affected. Simple reproduction: echo ACP initialize JSON with string protocolVersion piped to gemini --acp.

signals.topic: 搜索算法在小 limit 值下错误遗漏最高得分技能，CLI 用户持续获得劣质搜索结果

source_issues.title: bug: search misses highest-scoring skill when limit is small (vector candidate set too small)

signals.topic: Plugin fails to load when openclaw is globally installed on Windows due to module resolution failure
signals.summary: When openclaw is globally installed via npm on Windows, the plugin loader's resolveLoaderPluginSdkPackageRoot() cannot find the openclaw package root by traversing upward from the plugin directory, because the global npm install location is outside the plugin's parent directory tree. This causes subpath aliases like 'openclaw/plugin-sdk/channel-config-schema' to be missing, resulting in 'Cannot find module' errors that block all plugin loading.
aliases: global npm install plugin resolution failure on Windows
Cannot find module openclaw/plugin-sdk/channel-config-schema on Windows global install
signals.review_reason: This is a main-flow-blocking bug: plugin loading fails entirely for all Windows users who globally install openclaw via npm, which is a standard and expected installation method. The error is reproducible by the reporter with full steps, and the only workaround is a manual Windows junction creation — not a user-friendly solution. Count=1 (single repo) so P0 threshold not met, but the severity (complete plugin load failure for a standard install path on a major OS) justifies P1.

source_issues.title: [Bug] Plugin fails to load when openclaw is globally installed on Windows: Cannot find module 'openclaw/plugin-sdk/channel-config-schema'

signals.topic: Node Mode remains disconnected after gateway connection is established

signals.topic: Config schema mismatch silently blocks all UI config saves
