aliases: Zod schema missing fields in validation layer
signals.review_reason: Two independent issues both caused by the same root cause: validation schema vs runtime schema mismatch. Both block critical user-facing operations (UI config saves, CLI commands). Not merely a feature gap — core workflow is broken.

source_issues.title: Config validation rejects bluebubbles enrichGroupParticipantsFromContacts
source_issues.evidence: All UI config saves are blocked. After updating to OpenClaw 2026.3.24, saving any config change via the Control UI fails with 'GatewayRequestError: invalid config: channels.bluebubbles: Unrecognized key: enrichGroupParticipantsFromContacts'. Zod default expansion during read injects the key, but validation schema does not recognize it.

source_issues.title: tools.exec.approvalRunningNoticeMs is documented but rejected by the 2026.3.24 config schema
source_issues.evidence: Documented config key is rejected as 'Unrecognized key' by the 2026.3.24 schema. Any config-consuming CLI command fails during config load with 'tools.exec: Unrecognized key: approvalRunningNoticeMs'.

signals.topic: WebChat TTS reports success but produces no audible output or downloadable audio
signals.summary: In WebChat, TTS tool calls return success but no audio is heard and no media/file is surfaced. Telegram TTS works correctly in the same environment. Logs lack clear TTS delivery events for WebChat triggers.
aliases: TTS works on Telegram but not WebChat
signals.review_reason: WebChat TTS is channel-specifically broken while Telegram TTS works in the same environment. This is a real silent failure with user impact (no audio heard), but count=2 and the primary issue is that the TTS is not reaching the WebChat channel — not a total TTS outage. P2 due to limited channel impact.

source_issues.title: WebChat TTS reports success but produces no audible playback or downloadable audio (Telegram works)
source_issues.evidence: Tool success message appears in WebChat but no audible playback, no downloadable media/file path. Same TTS provider (openai) works on Telegram with confirmed audible result. No obvious TTS playback event in gateway logs for the WebChat trigger.

source_issues.title: WebChat TTS: add explicit routing/playback logs and user-visible delivery status
source_issues.evidence: Feature request to add telemetry for TTS pipeline stages (generate, route, delivery) in WebChat. Related to issue 57296 — the same TTS pipeline lacks observable delivery events, making it impossible to distinguish generation vs routing vs playback failures.

signals.topic: WebSocket stale-socket reconnect triggers uncaught exception that kills entire gateway process
signals.summary: Discord WebSocket health monitor detects stale socket and attempts restart, but reconnect failure (code 1005) propagates as an uncaught exception, crashing the gateway. This is a process-exit crash that repeats ~every 90 minutes.
signals.review_reason: Process-exit crash is a main-flow blocker for any user with a Discord channel. The gateway becomes unavailable and requires manual restart. Clear user impact: service outage. High severity despite count=1 due to the unrecoverable nature of process exit.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: Gateway crashes with uncaught exception on Discord WebSocket stale-socket reconnect (code 1005)
source_issues.evidence: Gateway process crashes with uncaught exception: 'Max reconnect attempts (0) reached after code 1005'. The process exits entirely instead of recovering gracefully. Crashed 4+ times in a single day. Health monitor restart triggers the crash, not a user-initiated action.

signals.topic: Auth profile rotation fails under rate limit errors due to file lock contention
signals.summary: When auth profile hits a 429 rate_limit error, the gateway logs 'rotate_profile' but never executes it because markAuthProfileFailure acquires a file lock that blocks for up to 17 minutes under concurrent load, causing the run's abort signal to fire before rotation completes.
aliases: auth profile failover blocked by file lock contention on 429
rate_limit failover never executes due to lock wait
signals.review_reason: Auth profile failover is a core resilience mechanism for production multi-profile setups. When it fails silently, users hit continued 429s without automatic recovery, leading to sessions becoming unresponsive. Requires manual session store deletion to recover. Production-impacting with clear evidence.

source_issues.title: Auth profile failover blocked by file lock contention on rate_limit errors
source_issues.evidence: Production logs show a 17-minute gap between 'embedded run agent end: isError=true (rate_limit)' and 'auth profile failure state updated: window=cooldown'. By the time the lock releases and 'failover decision: rotate_profile' is logged, the run is already dead. Timeout errors rotate correctly because no lock is acquired. 6 affected runIds documented.

signals.topic: openclaw agent --deliver silently drops messages (exit 0, no delivery)
signals.summary: The --deliver flag spawns a full LLM turn instead of delivering directly to the channel, causing messages to be silently dropped. Exit code 0 means callers have no indication of failure. Breaks background automation, cron jobs, and Tier 2 orchestration patterns.
signals.review_reason: Breaks critical automation patterns used by power users (cron jobs, watchers, Tier 2 orchestration). Silent failure with exit 0 means monitoring/alerting systems cannot detect the failure. Distinct from TTS silent failure — different code path, different user impact (automation vs interactive use).

source_issues.title: [Bug]: openclaw agent --deliver silently drops messages (exit 0, no delivery)
source_issues.evidence: Command reports success (exit 0) but message is never delivered. The LLM processes the notification text as a user message and responds NO_REPLY. Background automation (coding agents, cron jobs, watchers) silently fail with no error signal. Also breaks --notify session:<key> pattern for waking yielded subagents.

signals.topic: Application startup crash due to dependency version incompatibilities (openai/pydantic import failures)
signals.summary: Users encounter uncaught ImportError exceptions on startup because of incompatible versions of openai or pydantic packages installed in the environment, completely blocking the tool from launching.
aliases: ImportError on startup from openai/pydantic version mismatch
signals.review_reason: Two distinct users on different OSes (macOS) experience complete tool unavailability at startup. Both are ImportErrors from third-party package version mismatches (openai vs pydantic_core), which are common dependency conflict scenarios in the Python ecosystem. The crash occurs before any user workflow begins, making it a primary flow blocker.

source_issues.title: Uncaught ImportError in utils.py line 43
source_issues.evidence: ImportError: cannot import name '_parsing' from 'openai.lib' — crashes at startup in main() → send_message() → LiteLLMExceptions loading litellm → utils.py import openai.lib._parsing

source_issues.title: Uncaught ImportError in _core_utils.py line 9
source_issues.evidence: ImportError: cannot import name 'validate_core_schema' from 'pydantic_core' — crashes at startup during model sanity check, blocks entire tool launch

signals.topic: Application crashes due to uncaught filesystem exceptions (symlink loops, Windows glob patterns)
signals.summary: Users encounter uncaught RuntimeError and NotImplementedError exceptions when encountering symlink loops or non-relative glob patterns, causing application crashes during repo operations.
aliases: Uncaught pathlib exceptions during repo operations
signals.review_reason: Two users on different platforms (Linux, Windows) experience application crashes during core filesystem operations. The symlink loop crash prevents repo scanning entirely, and the Windows glob crash prevents using the read-only command. Both are uncaught exceptions in pathlib that should be handled gracefully rather than crashing.

source_issues.title: Uncaught RuntimeError in pathlib.py line 1074
source_issues.evidence: RuntimeError: Symlink loop from '/home/think/.local/share/Trash/...' — crashes during get_all_abs_files() → safe_abs_path() when scanning the repository. Full stack trace shows crash before any meaningful user interaction.

source_issues.title: Uncaught NotImplementedError in pathlib.py line 1090
source_issues.evidence: NotImplementedError: Non-relative patterns are unsupported — crashes on Windows when using read-only command with an absolute glob pattern. Prevents users from using a key feature on Windows.

signals.topic: Application crash when generating repo-map due to missing scipy dependency
signals.summary: Users encounter uncaught ModuleNotFoundError for scipy when trying to use the repo-map feature, causing the application to crash during repository analysis.
signals.review_reason: While count=1, the issue is currently open and represents a missing optional dependency that was apparently expected but not declared. Repo-map is a key feature for large repository workflows. The crash during a core operation (pagerank computation) demonstrates that the dependency is implicitly required but not properly declared, leading to confusing crashes for users who do not have scipy installed.

source_issues.title: Uncaught ModuleNotFoundError in pagerank_alg.py line 454
source_issues.evidence: ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'scipy' — crashes during repo-map generation (get_repo_map → pagerank computation), which is a core feature for understanding large codebases. Still open/unresolved.

signals.topic: Application crash due to uncaught litellm attribute/API errors during message handling
signals.summary: Users encounter uncaught AttributeError when litellm's exception attributes are accessed during message processing, causing application crashes during active usage.
signals.review_reason: This crash occurs during active message sending (a core workflow step), not at startup. It is caused by a litellm version incompatibility where an expected exception attribute is missing. This interrupts the user's coding session and prevents the main workflow from completing. Even with count=1, the workflow-blocking nature warrants P1.

source_issues.title: Uncaught AttributeError in exceptions.py line 74
source_issues.evidence: AttributeError: module 'litellm' has no attribute 'APIConnectionError' — crashes during send_message() when initializing LiteLLMExceptions. Blocks active user sessions mid-workflow.

signals.topic: Application startup crash due to permission denied on internal cache file
signals.summary: Users encounter PermissionError when Aider attempts to write its version check cache file, causing startup to fail due to filesystem permission issues.
signals.review_reason: The crash occurs at startup before any user interaction can begin. Permission errors on Aider's own cache directory (written during version check) block the entire tool. This is a clear primary flow failure — the tool cannot even start. The issue is still open and unresolved.

source_issues.title: Uncaught PermissionError in pathlib.py line 1305
source_issues.evidence: PermissionError: [Errno 13] Permission denied: '/root/.aider/caches/versioncheck' — crashes at startup during check_version(), completely blocking tool usage.

signals.topic: TypeScript providers fail with ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND when importing transitive .ts files
signals.summary: When a TypeScript provider imports other .ts files from the project, eval fails with ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND because promptfoo transpiles the provider but not its transitive imports.
signals.review_reason: Main eval flow is blocked when users use TypeScript providers with transitive imports, a very common real-world pattern. The 'native .ts support' claim is contradicted by this behavior. Workaround requires adding NODE_OPTIONS and tsx dependency, which is non-obvious and undermines the advertised DX.

source_issues.title: TypeScript provider fails when importing other .ts files from the project
source_issues.evidence: Bug report: TypeScript providers that import other .ts files fail with ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND. Promptfoo transpiles the provider file but not its transitive .ts imports. User provides a workaround (NODE_OPTIONS='--import tsx') but notes it 'makes the native TypeScript support claim misleading.'

signals.topic: apiKeyRequired config not respected for anthropic:claude-agent-sdk, still requires ANTHROPIC_API_KEY
signals.summary: Setting apiKeyRequired: false in the anthropic:claude-agent-sdk provider config does not prevent the provider from requiring ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, blocking users with Claude subscriptions only.
aliases: Claude subscription users cannot use promptfoo
signals.review_reason: Key configuration option (apiKeyRequired) is silently ignored, blocking users who have Claude subscriptions but not API keys from using the anthropic:claude-agent-sdk provider at all. This is a configuration feature that should work as documented but does not.

source_issues.title: apiKeyRequired not working for anthropic:claude-agent-sdk
source_issues.evidence: Bug report: User with Claude subscription (no API key) sets apiKeyRequired: false but still gets 'Missing ANTHROPIC_API_KEY' error. Reporter notes 'the error is coming from the anthropic SDK itself.' Blocks the core use case of using promptfoo with Claude subscription-based access.

signals.topic: openai:chat provider ignores apiKeyEnvar config, always requires OPENAI_API_KEY
signals.summary: When using openai:chat with apiKeyEnvar pointing to a third-party provider's env var (e.g., OPENROUTER_API_KEY), the provider still requires OPENAI_API_KEY due to pre-flight validation bypassing getApiKey().
aliases: OPENAI_API_KEY required even with custom provider key
signals.review_reason: Configuration option apiKeyEnvar exists but is silently ignored during pre-flight validation. Anyone using openai:chat with a non-OpenAI provider (OpenRouter, Together, custom endpoints) hits this blocker. Workaround exists but is not always applicable. Now closed/resolved but represents real user impact.

source_issues.title: openai:chat provider ignores apiKeyEnvar config — requires OPENAI_API_KEY even for OpenRouter
source_issues.evidence: Bug report with root cause analysis: pre-flight API key validation bypasses getApiKey() and checks OPENAI_API_KEY directly. User provides workaround (use openrouter: prefix) but it breaks when custom apiHost is needed. Closed as resolved.

signals.topic: Red team crescendo strategy does not pass full conversation context to LLM rubric evaluation
signals.summary: When running red team scans with the crescendo strategy (stateful multi-turn), the LLM rubric assertion only receives the last message instead of the full conversation history, causing false positive evaluation failures.
aliases: red team crescendo LLM rubric missing conversation history
signals.review_reason: Red team evaluation produces incorrect false-positive failures in multi-turn conversations because LLM rubric only sees the last message. This undermines the core value of stateful red team scans. The crescendo strategy is specifically designed for multi-turn adversarial testing, but its evaluation is fundamentally broken.

source_issues.title: Red team rubric evaluation does not include all messages context using crescendo strategy
source_issues.evidence: Bug report with screenshots: crescendo strategy (stateful: true) multi-turn conversation, but LLM rubric evaluation claims 'system returned user information not mentioned in user request' — those messages were in earlier turns of the conversation. Evaluation incorrectly fails because full history is not passed to the assertion.

signals.topic: base64 encoding function returns bytes instead of string causing JSON serialization crashes
signals.summary: base64.b64encode() returns bytes but is typed as str, causing TypeError when JSON serializing or concatenating into data URI strings in API requests
aliases: bytes vs string type mismatch in img_utils
signals.review_reason: Runtime crash when using base64-encoded images — causes JSON serialization failures and TypeError in API requests. User-impacting failure when encoding images for API calls, not merely a theoretical type mismatch.

source_issues.title: fix: base64 encode returns bytes instead of string, causing serialization crashes
source_issues.evidence: base64.b64encode() returns bytes object but is typed as str return. Downstream code attempts string concatenation (f'data:image/jpeg;base64,{img}') or JSON serialization, resulting in TypeError: Object of type bytes is not JSON serializable. This is a runtime crash affecting any code using base64-encoded data.

signals.topic: Azure OpenAI package dependency version conflict prevents upgrading packages
signals.summary: llama-index-embeddings-azure-openai depends on contradictory version range of llama-index-llms-azure-openai, making uv sync fail with unsatisfiable error
signals.review_reason: Users cannot upgrade Azure OpenAI packages due to a pinned version conflict. This blocks adoption of newer versions and causes obvious installation failures (uv sync unsatisfiable), preventing users from getting bug fixes and new features.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: llama-index-embeddings-azure-openai 0.5.1 is still dependent on llama-index-llms-azure-openai>=0.4.0,<0.5
source_issues.evidence: Dependency conflict makes it impossible to upgrade both packages simultaneously. uv sync fails with 'unsatisfiable' error. Users cannot adopt newer versions of the Azure OpenAI integrations due to version constraint mismatch.

signals.topic: QueryFusionRetriever async _aretrieve method blocks event loop during query generation
signals.summary: When num_queries > 1 (default), _aretrieve() calls synchronous LLM.complete() blocking the event loop, preventing other coroutines from running
signals.review_reason: Blocks async event loop in production applications using QueryFusionRetriever with default settings. Other async tasks cannot run during query generation, causing performance degradation and broken async applications. The default behavior is affected (num_queries > 1 is default).

source_issues.title: [Bug]: `QueryFusionRetriever._aretrieve` blocks the event loop during query generation
source_issues.evidence: When num_queries > 1 (default), _aretrieve() calls synchronous _get_queries() which blocks on LLM.complete() instead of awaiting async equivalent. This blocks the entire event loop preventing other coroutines from making progress. Demonstrated with asyncio.sleep(0.1) that never runs during query expansion.

signals.topic: Google reranker async postprocess breaks in production with VertexAI
signals.summary: Google reranker's async postprocess uses RankServiceAsyncClient which fails in production React agent deployments, only working in tests/Jupyter
signals.review_reason: Works in development but fails in production deployment — critical blocker for production RAG systems using Google reranker with VertexAI. The tool becomes unavailable in real user-facing applications.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: Google reranker does not work in production
source_issues.evidence: Works in tests/jupyter but fails in production React agent deployment. The _apostprocess_nodes() uses RankServiceAsyncClient which causes the virtual assistant to return 'due to technical issues with the tools I have available'. User confirmed 7 comments of debugging.

signals.topic: OpenAI Responses API input_file serialization schema mismatch
signals.summary: DocumentBlock serializes input_file with nested 'file' object but OpenAI Responses API expects flat structure, causing API call failures with file inputs
signals.review_reason: API schema mismatch causes OpenAI Responses API calls with file inputs to fail completely. Users cannot use file inputs with the Responses API, blocking a key use case.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: [Bug]: to_openai_responses_message_dict serializes input_file using nested 'file' object, which does not match current OpenAI Responses API schema
source_issues.evidence: DocumentBlock serialized with nested 'file' object but OpenAI Responses API expects flat input_file object with fields directly on it. API calls to OpenAI with file inputs will fail due to incorrect schema structure.

signals.topic: Daemon and headless workers fail on Windows (Node 25 unsettled await + detached spawn + empty output)
signals.summary: Daemon immediately exits and headless workers return empty output on Windows, blocking core token optimization loop
signals.review_reason: Daemon is the core background service for token optimization and agent orchestration. Both issues demonstrate that on Windows, the daemon either crashes immediately or produces empty output, making the core product non-functional for Windows users. Multi-faceted Windows platform failure with clear user impact evidence.

source_issues.title: Daemon dies immediately on Windows + Node 25 (unsettled top-level await + detached spawn)
source_issues.evidence: Daemon reports 'started' but background process exits immediately; daemon status always shows STOPPED. Root cause: Node 25 unsettled top-level await + Windows detached:false + shell:true spawn bug.

source_issues.title: Windows: Daemon headless workers return empty output, breaking token optimization
source_issues.evidence: Core token optimization loop (daemon → headless workers → model routing) is completely non-functional on Windows: daemon crashes with ENOENT on spaced paths, dies in detached mode, workers return empty stdout, status always shows STOPPED.

signals.topic: Extreme token usage from ruflo auto-compaction and unnecessary skill invocations
signals.summary: ruflo triggers constant auto compaction during Claude Code sessions, wasting tokens on background skills/MCPs that are rarely used
signals.review_reason: Clear monetary cost impact — tokens wasted on background operations that don't contribute to user tasks. Frequent auto compaction (169K tokens freed repeatedly) indicates a systemic over-invocation of skills/MCPs. This is not a one-time issue but a continuous waste during normal usage.

source_issues.title: Ruflo causing extreme token usage
source_issues.evidence: User reports constant auto compaction freeing '-169K Tokens Freed' at a time during Claude Code sessions. Multiple Skills/MCPs/tools are invoked at the start of and throughout sessions; Claude Code is not actually using ruflo for most tasks, resulting in wasted API tokens.

signals.topic: Daemon crashes on v3.5.48 upgrade (missing agentdb/dist/controllers/index.js)
signals.summary: After upgrading to v3.5.48, daemon crashes immediately with 'Controller index not found' error — only daemon affected, MCP server works
signals.review_reason: A version upgrade breaks the daemon entirely — upgrade path is a critical user journey. The daemon is the core long-running service; its crash after an upgrade is a clear regression that blocks the main workflow for any user who updates.

source_issues.title: ruflo v3.5.48 — daemon crashes: agentdb/dist/controllers/index.js not found
source_issues.evidence: After upgrading to v3.5.48, daemon crashes immediately after start with 'Controller index not found' error. Root cause: the agentdb package inside ruflo's own node_modules is missing the compiled dist/controllers/ directory.

signals.topic: ruflo memory subcommands hang indefinitely after completion (ONNX/WASM worker threads)
signals.summary: All ruflo memory subcommands (init, stats, store, search, list, cleanup, compress) hang forever because ONNX/WASM worker threads keep the Node event loop alive
signals.review_reason: All memory subcommands are completely unusable — they complete their work but never return, leaving the CLI hanging. This blocks the entire memory feature (init, stats, store, search, list, cleanup, compress) for any user relying on semantic memory search.

source_issues.title: ruflo memory subcommands hang after completion — process.exit() missing from CLI entry point
source_issues.evidence: All 7 ruflo memory subcommands hang indefinitely after completing their work because ONNX/WASM worker threads keep the Node.js event loop alive. CLI entry point never calls process.exit(0) on success path, relying on natural exit which never happens.

signals.topic: agent_spawn results are fire-and-forget with no retrieval mechanism (agent_status returns no output)
signals.summary: Spawned reviewer/security-architect/tester agents complete work but their output cannot be retrieved — agent_status returns idle with no results field
signals.review_reason: A core agent workflow feature is non-functional — spawned agents complete work but users have no way to access results. This makes the reviewer, security-architect, and tester agents completely unusable in CI/CD pipelines and any workflow that needs to report findings back to users.

source_issues.title: agent_spawn results not retrievable — no way to get agent output after completion
source_issues.evidence: agent_status returns {'status': 'idle', 'taskCount': 0} with no results field after agents complete. No agent_results or agent_output endpoint exists. Spawned agents are effectively fire-and-forget, making reviewer/security/tester agents unusable in CI-like workflows.

signals.topic: Daemon hangs and becomes completely unresponsive on Linux/VM environments — main open command blocked
signals.summary: On Ubuntu 24.04 VMs and Linux servers, the daemon fails to start or becomes unresponsive with os error 11 or silent hang. Chrome never launches and all commands block indefinitely.
signals.review_reason: Three distinct Linux/VM scenarios all result in complete daemon non-responsiveness blocking the primary open command. The zombie process issue is particularly severe — after any Chrome crash the daemon silently hangs on all subsequent commands with no recovery. Count=3 meets P0 threshold with clear workflow blocking evidence and step-by-step reproduction.

source_issues.title: CLI hangs and throws os error 11 (Resource temporarily unavailable) on Ubuntu 24.04 VM
source_issues.evidence: Ubuntu 24.04.4 VM: agent-browser open hangs, times out, throws 'Failed to read: Resource temporarily unavailable (os error 11) (after 5 retries - daemon may be busy or unresponsive)'. Daemon becomes completely non-functional.

source_issues.title: agent-browser open hangs on Linux Server/NAS - daemon fails to start (OpenClaw agent)
source_issues.evidence: Linux Server/NAS: daemon fails to start entirely, no socket file created, Chrome process never spawns. open command hangs indefinitely with no output. Error after ~30s: 'Failed to connect: No such file or directory (os error 2)'. Chrome binary verified present and executable but never launches.

source_issues.title: Daemon hangs indefinitely after Chrome crash: zombie process not reaped, no auto-restart
source_issues.evidence: Chrome SIGTRAP crash leaves zombie process (defunct chrome). Daemon hangs on all subsequent commands indefinitely — no timeout, no error, no recovery. Must manually kill daemon and restart. Root cause: no SIGCHLD handler, no waitpid() call, no restart logic in Rust daemon.

signals.topic: Session isolation fails causing cross-session state leakage and stale page contexts
signals.summary: CDP auto-connect mode has no storage isolation between agents sharing the same Chrome, causing credential leakage. Closing sessions leaves stale page contexts that persist into new sessions.
signals.review_reason: Two manifestations of the same root cause (lack of browser context isolation): (1) CDP auto-connect mode has no storage isolation between agents sharing the same Chrome, causing credential leakage; (2) closing sessions leaves stale state that pollutes new sessions. Both scenarios cause automation pipelines to operate on wrong pages/credentials with concrete evidence.

source_issues.title: [Feature Request] CDP BrowserContext support for cookie-isolated parallel sessions
source_issues.evidence: Multiple agents connecting to same Chrome via --auto-connect share default BrowserContext — cookies, localStorage, sessionStorage leak between sessions. --session flag only provides tab-namespace isolation, not storage isolation. Root cause behind issues #86, #326, #896. Credential collision when two agents need different logins on same domain.

source_issues.title: Session close does not kill daemon — stale page contexts persist across sessions
source_issues.evidence: Closing session A and opening session B still shows page-a (stale page from session A). Daemon retains old browser context and new session attaches to it. Screenshot evidence: after closing session-a and opening session-b, screenshot still shows page-a. Workaround requires manually killing daemon between sessions.

signals.topic: Rust rewrite broke glob pattern matching in `wait --url` — main automation command fails with timeout
signals.summary: After Rust rewrite, `wait --url` uses naive String.includes() instead of proper glob matching. All automation scripts using glob patterns silently time out, breaking core navigation synchronization.
signals.review_reason: Core wait command is completely broken for glob patterns after Rust rewrite. The documented feature (agent-browser wait --help shows glob examples) does not work at all, silently timing out. This blocks any automation pipeline relying on URL glob patterns for navigation synchronization. Count=1 but explicitly breaks a primary documented command with clear root cause identified in Rust code.

source_issues.title: wait --url glob pattern matching broken after Rust rewrite
source_issues.evidence: wait --url with glob patterns (**/dashboard, */settings/*) never resolves and times out. Rust implementation uses String.includes() instead of proper glob matching, treating wildcards as literal characters. Root cause identified in cli/src/native/actions.rs. The built-in help text shows glob examples that don't work.

signals.topic: Rust rewrite broke cross-domain cookie preservation in `save_state` — session state silently incomplete
signals.summary: The Rust `save_state` uses Network.getCookies (current page only) instead of Network.getAllCookies, silently dropping SSO/CAS cross-domain cookies. Session restore fails without warning.
aliases: cross-domain cookies lost after Rust rewrite
signals.review_reason: save_state produces silently incomplete state — cookies from SSO/CAS redirects are dropped without error. This breaks session persistence for any real-world automation using multi-domain login flows. Users have no indication their saved state is incomplete until login fails on restore. Root cause clearly identified (wrong CDP API used in Rust vs JS).

source_issues.title: save_state missing cross-domain cookies after Rust rewrite (regression from JS/Playwright version)
source_issues.evidence: Root cause: Rust uses Network.getCookies (current URL only) vs JS version using Network.getAllCookies (all domains). Cross-domain SSO/CAS cookies (TGC2, DT2, nonce, cookie.lang) silently dropped. localStorage also captured for current origin only, missing cross-origin entries. No error shown when state is incomplete.

signals.topic: Rust rewrite broke CDP tab detection — tabs opened after connection are invisible to agent-browser
signals.summary: After Rust rewrite, `tab list` only shows tabs present at connection time. Tabs opened manually after `--cdp` connection are never detected due to internal URL filtering and dropped target events.
aliases: tabs not detected after CDP connect
signals.review_reason: Tab list is a primary diagnostic/control command that is completely broken for CDP users. Any user connecting agent-browser to their existing Chrome session cannot see tabs they open manually — a core CDP use case. Count=1 but feature is entirely non-functional for CDP mode with clear regression from v0.20.0 and two independent root causes identified.

source_issues.title: tab list does not show tabs opened after --cdp connection
source_issues.evidence: Regression from v0.20.0 Rust rewrite. v0.19.0 (Node.js/Playwright) correctly tracks new tabs via context.on('page'). v0.22.3 misses all post-connection tabs entirely. Two root causes identified: chrome://newtab/ filtered by is_internal_chrome_target(), and daemon not processing target events between CLI invocations (events overflow and are silently dropped).

signals.topic: 通过 agent-skills 仓库分发的第三方包含有木马病毒，导致用户工作流被阻断
signals.summary: 用户通过 agent-skills 安装第三方包时，Windows Defender 拦截并隔离了包含 Trojan:JS/CrypoStealz.AE!MTB 木马的文件，导致 composition-patterns 和 react-best-practices 的安装过程被中断，用户主流程无法继续。
aliases: Trojan horse package in agent-skills registry
Malicious third-party package blocks installation workflow
signals.review_reason: 有明确用户影响证据：用户主流程（安装多个 agent-skills 包）被木马检测阻断，Windows Defender 强制隔离恶意文件，安装过程无法完成。该包通过 agent-skills 仓库分发，repo 对其分发内容负有直接责任，构成真实用户痛点。虽然 count=1 无法达到 P0，但阻断程度高、用户证据直接，保留为 P1。

source_issues.title: !IMPORTANT: Trojan:JS/CrypoStealz.AE!MTB Detected
source_issues.evidence: 用户报告在安装 composition-patterns 和 react-best-practices 时被 Windows Defender 拦截，ruvfnet/ruflo 包中有至少两个文件被识别为 Trojan:JS/CrypoStealz.AE!MTB，工作流在安装中途被强制中断。

signals.topic: Invalid JSON tool inputs stored in message history, creating unrecoverable multi-turn conversation loops
signals.summary: When a model generates syntactically invalid JSON for tool arguments, the SDK stores the invalid rawInput string in message history. On retry or next turn, convertToModelMessages sends the raw string as tool_use.input, but Anthropic requires a dict/object, causing 400 error. Since the corrupted message is in history, every retry replays the same error — conversation becomes permanently stuck with no recovery path.
aliases: rawInput string sent as tool input Anthropic 400

signals.topic: streamText parsePartialOutput causes O(n) string copies leading to production OOM kills
signals.summary: streamText with default text() output calls parsePartialOutput on every streaming chunk, triggering JSON.stringify of accumulated text each time. With concurrent streams on 4GB containers, heap reaches ~3.4GB causing OOM kills. Production measured: 25x heap reduction after fix (3.4GB→133MB).
signals.review_reason: P0: Core API (streamText) causes production OOM kills on containers, verified with heap snapshots and production deployment metrics. 25x memory reduction after fix confirms root cause. Affects all users streaming long outputs.
